column2: Change first, then chat in a room.
After quickly changing clothes, I paced restlessly around the room.
Maybe she thinks I'm a safe guy.
The door clicked open, and {n2} came in.
it's the same as my room.”
{n2} stated the obvious and plopped down on the bed with a bounce.
why are you just standing there?”
Hiding my inner turmoil, I sat on the other bed.
well, I'm really worn out.{r}{p}My legs and hips are shot.”
“That's because you're not used to it.
Just watching her ski, you could see {n2} used no unnecessary force at all.
“Want me to give you a massage?{r}{p}I'm good at it.”
{n2} climbed onto my bed without waiting for an answer.
I lay down as told, and {n2} started kneading my calves with both hands.
{n2}'s supple hands slid from my calves up to my thighs.
You don't have to be shy.”
If we stayed alone in the room like this, I'd lose my reason.
Was it my imagination, or did {n2}'s reply sound a bit disappointed…?
Telling myself that, I went down to the common room.
Could we get a picture with you?”
One of the trio, a girl with glasses, spoke to us, holding out a camera.
This is why good looks are such a burden….
With that thought, I stood and approached the girl.
sure, I don't mind.{r}{p}Now, what pose…”
But the girl with glasses hurriedly held me back.
the manager doesn't need to be in it.”
“You're the actress Takeko Matsu, aren't you?{r}{p}You know, from 'Lingerie Nation'…”
Amazingly, the one they wanted a photo of was {n2}!
She'd been mistaken for the lead of a drama about the lingerie industry called 'Lingerie Nation'.
The girl with glasses handed me the camera.
Just press the button, right? Just press the button.
I pressed the shutter right on the “z” at the end of “cheese.”
They probably all came out with goofy faces.
…Unaware of my little spite, {n2} and the others laughed together.
They already seemed to be good friends.
“Oh, so I was wrong.{r}{p}I was so sure…”
it's Aki's fault for getting the wrong idea…”
The long-haired girl poked the girl with glasses.
Taking back the camera, the girls bowed to me.
“Oh, that's fine.{r}{p}I don't mind at all.”
I said what I didn't mean.
“But you're so pretty, {n2}, so we just…”
Hearing it put that way didn't feel bad.
As we chatted, introductions started naturally.
I never said that!{r}{p}You're pretty enough, {n2}…”
She didn't even listen to me and strode into the dining room.
{n2} blushed faintly, looked away, and hurriedly stood up.
The knives and forks were already set out on the dining room table.
The trio of girls and the couple who had just arrived were already seated.
We took a table for two as well.
In the middle of the table stood a candle shaped like a Christmas tree.
Its tiny flame flickered in {n2}'s downcast eyes too.
Her beautiful hand rested in the middle of the table as if inviting me.
To distract myself from wanting to touch her hand, I started on an unrelated topic.
“…In Euclidean geometry, a straight line between two points is uniquely determined, but in non-Euclidean geometry there are infinitely many…”
talking math in a place like this.”
While I was thinking of another topic, the food arrived.
Without realizing it, I had gently touched her hand.
The instant our hands touched, {n2} flinched, but she didn't pull her hand away.
The people around us stared, wondering what was going on.
kidding! I was kidding!{r}{p}Of course I was kidding!
I laughed it off, and then the food arrived.
I said with a sly grin.
I had apparently made a mistake and been stroking an ashtray shaped like a white seashell.
To cover my embarrassment, I looked around.
“…If I disliked you, I wouldn't have come to a place like this with you.”
She nodded, so faintly you'd have missed it if you weren't paying attention.
Ever since she'd invited me skiing, I'd half hoped for this….
Now that I knew her feelings for sure, I was walking on air.
I couldn't tell what the food tasted like, or what was going on around me.
{n2} was right in front of me.
Before I knew it, an empty coffee cup sat in front of me.
And only now did I notice there was a very strange guest here.
In the corner of the dining room, blending into the wall, sat a man in a coat.
Even at mealtime he hadn't taken off his jacket or hat, and he was even wearing black sunglasses.
He didn't look like a skier, or even a salesman here on business.
But would a yakuza come to a place like this…?
Now that I knew {n2}'s feelings for sure, none of that mattered.
Yakuza or mafia, I didn't care.
“Shall we go to the common room?”
But rather than that, want to go night skiing?”
I summoned my courage and said it.
Leaving the dining room, I passed the three office ladies at the front desk making a fuss about being peeped at or something, ignored them, and went up to the second floor.
I let {n2} into the room first, closed the door behind me, and quietly locked it.
As I gently pulled her close, she closed her eyes.
Then I caught a glimpse of something outside the window.
My heart jumped and I strained my eyes.
just now, there was someone outside the window.”
Now that she said it, she was right.
Fearfully, I approached the window and brought my face close to the glass to look out.
All I could see was snow swirling in the light from inside.
I steeled myself and opened the window.
I stuck my head out and looked all around.
Whether from the cold or from unease, a shiver ran down my spine.
didn't someone downstairs say something about being peeped at?”
“But it's strange for anyone to be outside in this blizzard, and how would they have peeked into the second floor?”
“Let's go downstairs and hear what's going on.”
Downstairs, Mr. Kobayashi was earnestly explaining something to the office ladies.
“In this blizzard, and on the second floor? Maybe you mistook a tree branch or something?”
“I did not mistake it!{r}{p}There was a person outside the window.”
I poked my head out from behind the girl with glasses, who kept insisting.
I just saw it too.{r}{p}It was the shadow of a person.”
You too? What are you saying!{r}{p}It's an optical illusion.
Mr. Kobayashi said it with a laugh, but his eyes weren't laughing at all.
It doesn't suit you at all, so you should stop.”
Embarrassed, I looked around to hide it.
And what would a yakuza be doing alone at an inn?”
Looking closer, he was quietly sipping his soup, and maybe he was actually a nice guy, despite his looks.
Maybe he kept the sunglasses on just to look cool, or maybe his eyes were so mean-looking that people got scared.
Either way, by the time the food was set out, I'd forgotten all about it.
{n2} took a sip from her bowl and let out an exclamation.
It must have been that dish called kenchin-jiru, a soup full of julienned vegetables.
That piping-hot soup was truly delicious, and it felt like it warmed my body from
The dishes that followed were all satisfying in both flavor and portion, and sighs of contentment could be heard from here and there.
I thought again that this place could make it as a restaurant, not just an inn.
In fact, that yakuza-looking man and the middle-aged couple might have come just for the food.
“I hate to say it, but what Auntie makes is hardly what you'd call cooking….”
{n2} glanced around carefully and began to speak in a low voice.
“It's my uncle who loves cooking.{r}{p}He's wanted to be a chef since he was a kid.”
“He gave it up once and became a lawyer, but he couldn't let go of the dream.{r}{p}Partly because they couldn't have kids, he closed his office and started an inn.”
Swapping a book of law for a kitchen knife….
“I guess.{r}{p}But it so happens that my grandfather, my mother's father, that is…”
She picked up the glass on the table.
I urged her to go on.
{n2} took a sip of water and continued.
“Grandpa owned several mountains around here.{r}{p}They say the land was there from the start.{r}{p}So money wasn't much of a struggle, financially and all.”
“Isn't your uncle an idiot?{r}{p}If it were me, I'd have stayed a lawyer.”
“Don't say it like that.{r}{p}He agonized over it in his own way, you know.”
I seemed to have made her angry.
“No, no, I didn't mean it that way… well… how to put it…{p}By the way, did you know that 'baka', as in 'idiot' in Japanese, sounds just like 'vaca', the Spanish word for cow?”
I changed the subject to wriggle out of it.
{n2}'s uncle is really admirable! A man who chases his dreams just shines!”
I don't think he's quite that great, but…”
“No, from the first time I saw him, I thought he was a cut above.{r}{p}As expected of {n2}'s uncle.”
Phew, she seemed to have finally recovered her mood.
I breathed a sigh of relief inwardly.
“It must have been really hard when he changed careers.”
then you can go home first by yourself, {n1}.{r}{p}I'm staying.”
“But can I even get home alone in the snow…?”
“Just crawl home if you have to.{r}{p}Hey, Toshio,
In a coaxing voice, {n2} reached for Toshio's arm.
“Oh right, my part-time job is off tomorrow! Whoa, I totally forgot.{r}{p}Geez, my memory's been terrible lately….”
I hurriedly stood up, took {n2}'s arm, and pulled her to her feet.
I dragged {n2} out of the dining room.
Mr. Kobayashi's expression changed, so I hurriedly took it back.
“…Don't tell the other guests.{r}{p}They definitely wouldn't like it.”
For a business like this, even a prank like that might be no joke.
I smirked, thinking I wouldn't have to job hunt now.
But Mr. Kayama didn't seem to be listening.
“Everybody's making a fuss about the recession these days.{r}{p}Not us, though.{r}{p}'Cause we only hire folks with real ability.{r}{p}We run on merit, see.
So what d'ya say, come work for us?”
Mr. Kobayashi and {n2} just watched, grinning.
“On second thought, let me think it over.”
But Mr. Kayama still wasn't listening.
Glad you said so.{r}{p}Once it's decided, no time like the present.{r}{p}We run on merit, you know.
Education doesn't matter, so you don't need to graduate.{r}{p}Let's get you back to Osaka and working right away.”
Now I wouldn't need to earn credits or write a graduation thesis.
“You're quitting school and going to Osaka?
…Then we won't be able to see each other anymore.”
On second thought, I'm not quite…”
But Mr. Kayama wouldn't let me off.
A man takes back what he's said?!{r}{p}No way, that won't do.
marry me and come to Osaka with me!”
If you want to go, go by yourself.”
…And when the dreamlike trip ended, I submitted my withdrawal papers and left for Osaka alone.
I never saw {n2} again, and twenty years passed.
President Kayama's health failed and he retired; now I run the company.
It's a small company, so I'm far from a millionaire, and the days are busy, but I'm content enough.
I married and have two children.
And now my wife and I drove out to the inn of my memories.
As I stepped through the front door, a nostalgic voice called out.
Mr. Kobayashi's hair was completely white now.
I thought I was gonna die.{r}{p}A terrible blizzard started up on me.”
As I said that, a strange feeling washed over me.
No, it must be my imagination.
never dreamed I'd be caught up in a horrifying murder
so that applies to me too, doesn't it?”
I coughed hard to cover it up.
“There was a cockroach in the soup.”
Mr. Mikimoto's eyes went round in surprise.
I thought I'd picked it out before serving….”
you all fall for it so easily….”
Mr. Kobayashi waved his hands, clowning.
Keiko put a hand on her chest in relief.
I had five refills of that soup….”
No, no.{r}{p}I'm a guest.{r}{p}I arrived late, so I missed dinner, though….{r}{p}Might as well introduce myself properly.
There are quite a few young women here, after all.”
Saying so, Mr. Mikimoto set down his teacup and took on a slightly formal tone.
“The ultimate luxury is, without question, eating hot pot in midsummer with the air conditioner blasting.”
It's burning a stove at full blast in Antarctica and eating ice pops.”
It's getting into a freezer at the equator and then…”
Give it a rest!{r}{p}Why would you need to get in a freezer?
Besides the common room, the first floor has…
The staff room for Midori, Toshio and the others.
The drying room and so on.
We checked them one by one.
When Mr. Kobayashi gripped the knob, Mr. Mikimoto and I readied our “weapons.”
The moment we both nodded, Mr. Kobayashi flung the door open and hid behind it.
Then we went in, thrusting out the ski pole and the mop
That way we searched every room, even under the beds.
Since having everyone enter one room might let someone slip away in the meantime, only Mr. Mikimoto and I went inside.
At first we were terrified, but as we repeated the same thing, we gradually grew bolder.
Mr. Mikimoto seemed to feel the same; his color had returned to normal.
“No matter who comes out, w-with five of us, we'll be fine, right?”
There are five of us, after all.”
There was no sign of anyone on the first floor.
Being closer to the scene, it felt more dangerous.
Everyone had probably begun to think the culprit was unlikely to have gotten in.
Unlike before, they went up to the second floor completely relaxed.
“I'll have you know, I did judo in high school.{r}{p}If the culprit shows up, I'll throw him with a shoulder throw, pin him down, and he won't be able to make a peep.”
Mr. Kayama only came out with this now.
I held back from saying that in that case he should lead the way.
Upstairs, we checked the guest rooms the same way as before.
…But again, not even a mouse was hiding under the beds or in the closets.
Mr. Kayama asked, pointing at the door at the end of the hallway.
“That's a storeroom for cleaning supplies and such.{r}{p}A person…
could hide in there, I suppose, but…”
As we approached, we clearly heard a rustling sound.
Mr. Mikimoto rolled his eyes toward me.
That was what his eyes said.
Sweat seeped into the hand gripping the ski pole.
Mr. Kobayashi, hand on the knob, looked around at everyone.
Me, Mr. Mikimoto, Toshio, and, from a bit farther back, Mr. Kayama.
The four of us nodded at once.
The instant I heard a thud, the door burst open and a black shape leapt out!
“The cat they keep here.{r}{p}I hadn't seen her around and wondered where she'd gone.{r}{p}Never thought she'd be in here.”
I kept quiet, though I was annoyed.
I kept quiet, intending to stay by {n2}.
“You're coming too, right, Mr. Kayama?{r}{p}If we run into the culprit outside, you'll hit him with your judo Hell Wheel, won't you?”
well, sure.{r}{p}…But it's cold out there.{r}{p}I,
I'm no good with the cold.{r}{p}If you find him, drive him inside.{r}{p}I'll give him my Swallow Reversal.”
He sounded like the monk Ikkyu {C3}(clever monk from folk tales){C0}.
Besides, I don't think Swallow Reversal is a judo technique….
In the end, Mr. Kobayashi, Toshio and Mr. Mikimoto decided to look around outside.
The three went back to their rooms to change and came down about five minutes later.
We watched anxiously as the three, wearing ski clothes and armed with “weapons,” headed out.
{n2} said something ominous under her breath.
“What if the culprit is still nearby…”
No one's going to stand around outside in this blizzard.{r}{p}He's long gone.”
Even so, waiting inside only made the anxiety grow.
I even began to think it would have been easier to go out with them.
it might work, so let's at least try!”
I remembered Mr. Kobayashi saying 'cell phones don't work here,' but I deliberately didn't speak up.
After Mr. Kayama went upstairs, I was the only man left.
“W-we're going to the restroom for a bit.”
Aki said, and the three of them went up to the second floor in a huddle.
Just as they disappeared from view, a bell buzzed from somewhere.
{n2} and I exchanged glances, stood, and ran after her.
By the time we reached the back door, Kyoko had just fearfully opened it.
Snow and wind blew in, and then an enormous lump of snow came tumbling in.
Kyoko let out a stifled scream.
Looking closely after calming down, it was Mr. Kobayashi and the others who had gone out earlier.
Covered in snow, piled up like dumplings.
Mr. Kobayashi was gasping for breath.
Sure enough, bright red blood was caked at Mr. Mikimoto's temple.
Kyoko recovered from her shock and began giving orders briskly.
“Anyway, let's get him to a bed.{r}{p}Midori, get the first aid kit….”
Take that side.{r}{p}Don't move him too suddenly….”
Mr. Kobayashi and I carried Mr. Mikimoto
to his own room on the second floor.
We took off his jacket and laid him on the bed.
Midori and Kyoko, who'd brought the first aid kit, disinfected the wound and applied gauze deftly.
There was nothing more I could do, so I left the room.
I ran into Mr. Kayama in the hallway just as he came out of his room, and we talked as we went down the stairs.
Oh, the cell phone.{r}{p}No good, no good.
In the common room, only Haruko and {n2} sat there worriedly.
Mr. Kayama didn't seem to have been told anything yet.
the thing is, nobody saw it,
He seemed to swallow the word “dead.”
Mr. and Mrs. Kobayashi and Midori should be treating him now, but…”
“Surely he's not planning to kill us one by one, is he?”
This old guy comes out with outrageous things again.
Both {n2} and Haruko flinched for a moment.
“Well, if they killed us all, they could wait for the blizzard to pass in peace in here.{r}{p}And with nobody left to call the police, they'd have plenty of time to think about how to escape.”
Fleeing through this snow was suicidal, but hiding for now and waiting for someone to come outside made sense.
Maybe Mr. Mikimoto was targeted simply because he was the first one in sight.
Though I was beginning to half believe the possibility myself, I said so because I didn't want her to worry.
even if that's so, we'll be fine as long as we don't go outside again.{r}{p}If we stay together and never get left alone.”
But my attempt to reassure her didn't seem to work very well.
“That's easy to say, but the phones don't work, and how are we supposed to call for help without going outside?”
“Anyway, if we hold out until morning, we'll be fine.{r}{p}No one could survive till morning in that cold.”
“…Then all the more reason he'd attack us like a desperate man.”
Just as {n2} said that, the Kobayashis came down from the second floor.
His expression was dark, so I wondered if it was serious, but that wasn't it.
“He says he didn't see anything.{r}{p}Apparently he was hit suddenly from out of nowhere.”
Mr. Kobayashi's expression seemed to be due to not knowing who the culprit was.
“Situation, well, in that blizzard….{r}{p}Anyway, we went outside and quickly got separated from the other two.{r}{p}By the time I found him again, he was lying there.”
That meant that when Mr. Mikimoto was attacked, the only one with him was Toshio.
Toshio hit Mr. Mikimoto from behind…?
I suppressed the suspicion welling up and asked Mr. Kobayashi.
“…Hard to say.{r}{p}He said he was dizzy, so he might have a concussion….{r}{p}But only a doctor could tell.{r}{p}At least,
it doesn't look like his skull is cracked or anything….”
“When I saw him earlier, I'm pretty sure he was bleeding from the head…{p}Was it the left or the right?”
Around the right temple…{p}why, is something wrong?”
“So he was hit on the right temple from behind.{r}{p}Which means the culprit is right-handed.”
While they were talking, Toshio arrived.
He sat on the sofa and asked Mr. Kobayashi.
“To a layman's eye it doesn't look like much, but if he's bleeding in the brain he could just drop dead by morning, so we can't relax.”
For no particular reason I headed left.
The building should be on the left, I believed, and while I walked desperately, a white wall suddenly appeared before me.
Shouting, I moved forward along the wall.
The wall I was touching with my left hand suddenly vanished.
I knew right away I had reached the corner of the building, but I still couldn't suppress my fear.
If I just turn left, it should be fine….
Believing so, I walked through the snow as if swimming.
No matter how far I went, I couldn't see anything but snow.
I felt it must be the other way after all.
…I no longer knew what to do.
For what felt like an eternity, I wandered through the snow.
Then, thinking I heard a voice from far away, I stopped and listened.
But I couldn't tell where it was coming from.
I managed to get a rough sense of the direction.
Hiding my unease, I chided Mr. Kayama.
It was something I didn't want to think about too closely.
“That's impossible, no matter what.{r}{p}Even if you were very efficient, it'd take thirty minutes, wouldn't it?”
At Mr. Kobayashi's words, everyone nodded.
Normally that would be the main reason.
But this time Mr. Tanaka was killed in his own room, so that reason hardly applied.
I decided to check whether the bathtub had been used.
The bathtub wasn't wet and showed no sign of having been used at all.
A thought was beginning to take shape in my head.
“…Let's go back to the common room.”
I announced it, and left the room without waiting for a reply.
Back in the common room, I said.
Isn't it a different person from whoever killed Mr. Tanaka?”
“…Probably, yes.{r}{p}Since most of us couldn't have killed Mr. Tanaka.”
so what you're saying is I didn't kill Midori, but I killed Mr. Tanaka?”
I didn't kill Midori or Mr. Tanaka!”
Toshio's eyes didn't look like he was lying.
Besides, it was unnatural to think Midori and Mr. Tanaka were killed by different people.
Then another thought flashed into my mind like a revelation.
Who killed Midori and Mr. Tanaka.”
I didn't answer right away and began speaking to everyone.
“Even if you say that won't do…
my idea is what I said earlier.{r}{p}You all can judge whether you think it's right.”
At my words, everyone exchanged glances.
{n2} was the one to break the ice.
“I believe your deduction, {n1}.{r}{p}Because I can't think of anything else.”
hold on a minute.{r}{p}You're not gonna decide by majority vote or something, are you?”
that might be fine, but let's do this as a trial.{r}{p}We're citizens of a democracy, after all.”
Toshio smiled with a twist of his mouth.
{n1} is the prosecutor and we're the jury.{r}{p}The defense can be the man himself or his wife.{r}{p}If we reach a unanimous guilty verdict, then…”
you can't mean you'll kill me…”
“I'd like to, but the most we can do is lock him up.”
Toshio said regretfully, and Mr. Kayama looked relieved.
that settles it for you, do what you like.”
It was sudden, but everyone was watching me with serious faces.
I had no choice but to start in a tone I'd seen in dramas.
I hereby charge Mr. Seiichi Kayama,
Tanaka, what was the first name?{r}{p}Never mind…
of Mr. Tanaka, and of Midori Shinozaki…”
and, uh, for assaulting me too…”
“…and I'd like to accuse him of assault and battery on Mr. Mikimoto as well.”

“I explained most of it earlier, so I'll just summarize the key points.{r}{p}The only person who could have killed Mr. Tanaka and also hit Mr. Mikimoto was Mr. Kayama.{r}{p}Therefore I believe Mr. Kayama is the culprit.”
“Mr. Kayama, do you plead not guilty?”
You think I'll keep up this charade?{r}{p}I didn't do it, and that's that.
That's all I've got to say.”
Then let's take a verdict.{r}{p}Who thinks he's guilty?”
Even as he said it, Toshio raised his own hand.
{n2} raised hers, and I reluctantly followed suit.
Gradually, hesitantly, everyone raised their hands.
Aside from Haruko, Mr. Kayama's wife, the only ones not raising their hands were the Kobayashis.
Mr. Kayama raised his hand vigorously, but surprisingly, Haruko and the Kobayashis didn't raise theirs this time either.
When Toshio asked, Mr. Kobayashi answered with a grimace.
…It means I can't judge either way.”
Toshio asked in surprise, and Haruko looked away from her husband and bit her lip.
Don't tell me you don't trust me.{r}{p}Huh?
Haruko kept her head down and didn't answer.
Toshio chose not to press and seemed to decide to settle it.
“…We can count the three as abstentions.{r}{p}It's decided: unanimous guilty verdict.”
